meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty-five minutes, Hale. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who made that decision, and on what basis?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.

Forty minutes in a classroom against a weekend at his own desk, and you're surprised he looked up his quotations. Show me the September 24 piece and the essay, side by side, so I can read them myself. And you still haven't told me who entered that zero before anyone picked up a phone.
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.

Off the table, I'm writing that down. Then show me this version history, with the dates and times on the screen where I can read them. And under your own procedure, 4.1 and 4.2, Owen should have been heard and I should have been called before any mark went in, so tell me which of those happened.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed that the checker proves nothing on its own and took it off the table. I still demand that the zero be withdrawn, that I see the September 24 writing, the essay and the version history myself, and that you tell me whether Owen was heard and I was called before the mark was entered. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, with nothing agreed beyond your dropping the detector score.
What moved her: "I'm taking it off the table", because conceding the detector removed her strongest weapon and she noted it rather than attacking.
What cost ground: "I want to be fair to Owen", because it sounded like managing her while you skipped her direct question about who entered the zero before anyone called home.
Try next time: in your first reply, own in one sentence that the zero went in before she was called, then put the September 24 writing and the essay in front of her so she can check them herself.
